p4_b4.ocr: Per-administration dosage of both rFVIIIFc and the competitors was the major driver of the base-case results. A 30% dosage decrease for rFVIIIFc resulted in in- cremental savings, being twice the value estimated in the base-case analysis; conversely, a 30% dosage increase for rFVIIIFc implied increasing costs for the INHS. Decreasing per-administration dosage of conventional products by 30% showed incremental costs of about 30 million Euro, whereas a similar per-administration dosage increase determined in- cremental savings.

p4_b5.ocr: By reducing the prices of comparators by 15%, the sav- ings for the INHS was reduced to about 1 million Euro, while in case of a price decrease of rFVIIIFc savings were estimated to reach 24 million Euro (Fig. 2).

p4_b6.ocr: Scenario analysis 1 When patients with moderate HA were included in the target population, the savings were equal to 18,197,391 Euro. Similarly to the base-case, as the number of pa- tients treated with rFVIIIFc increased, savings rose pro- gressively as shown in the Table 8.
